Order 
This miscellaneous appeal by appellant/claimant under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act.

1988 is arising out of the Award dated 16-02-2022 passed by 20th Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (hereinafter it would be referred to as "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.1939 of 2017 seeking enhancement of compensation amount.

2. The date of accident, negligence and issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.
3.

As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal, for the injuries sustained by NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35304 2 MA-3754-2023 appellant- claimant Ashok in the alleged accident,
the Claims Tribunal on the basis of documents and material available on record, has awarded a total lump sum amount of Rs. 40,558/- with interest @ 6% per annum in favour of Claimant from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the appellants contends that the Claims Tribunal has committed an error in holding that that there is no permanent disability of appellant- claimant caused due to the accident,
although the appellant had produced the documentary evidence which clearly shows that he had sustained fracture of condyle bone of right leg.
On behalf of appellant, Dr.Kush Bandi has been examined as PW2, who clearly proved the permanent disability to the extent of 11% as per medical document Ex.P16.
Due to alleged accident, the appellant is unable to do his profession as driving

The Claims Tribunal has committed an error in awarding Rs.30,000/- towards transportation,
special diet and attendance expenses looking to the nature of injuries sustained by the appellant.
The Claims Tribunal has only assessed the income of appellant at Rs. 2,000/- per month which is on the lower side.
Hence, prayed for enhancement of proper compensation amount in favour of claimant.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for Insurance Company as well as learned counsel appearing for owner of the offending vehicle has argued in support of the impugned Award and contended that Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case, which does not call for any interference by this Court.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.

So far as income of the claimant is concerned,
as per the evidence that came on record, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35304 3 MA-3754-2023 he was a driver by profession, aged around 35 years, therefore, in view of Minimum Wages Act, his income should be assessed as Rs.6,000/- per month.
Therefore, his income is fixed as Rs.6,000/- per month instead of Rs.2,000/- per month as assessed by the Claims Tribunal.

8. On perusal of medical documents produced on behalf of appellant before the Claims Tribunal and looking to the injuries sustained by the appellant, especially the permanent disability certificate produced by doctor concerned, this Court thinks it appropriate to award the compensation by modifying as under:-
HEAD AMOUNT

Monthly income Rs.6,000/- x12+40% x5% (PDS)x16 Other Heads:-
 Pain and suffering Rs. 10,0
Medical expenses Rs. 5,00

sentences.text: Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs. 1,21,198/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs.40,558/- Accordingly, the appellant/claimant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.80,640/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
10. In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.80,640/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35304 4 MA-3754-2023 as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

11. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellant- claimant within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
12. In view of above, miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellants- claimants stands disposed of.
